### page_2
A palaeomagnetic study of Svecokarelian basic rocks from
northern Sweden
STEN-AKEE LMING
Elming, S.-A.. 1985 11 30: A palaeomagnetic study of Svecokarelian basic rocks from
northern Sweden. Geologiska Fiireniiigens i Stockholm Fiirliatidliiigar, Vol. 107, Pt. 1, pp.
17-35. Stockholm. ISSN 0016-7S6X.
This palaeornagnetic investigation comprises basic rocks from six localities from the Sveco-
karelian zone in northern Sweden. htost of the pole positions in this study and other
reported poles of Svecokarelian and post-Svecokarclian rocks fall within an approximately
12 degrees wid-e band running from east to west representing ages of magnetizations from
18SO-1700 to 1530 hla. Thermal demagnetizations of specimens of the probably oldest
massifs indicate a possible backward continuation of the polar wandering path. hlineralogi-
cal studies of thin sections of the rocks show ore symplectites and myrmekitic textures
indicating a slow rate of cooling at least at the end of the rock formation. Signs of
metamorphism are demonstrated by the existencc of secondary minerals, including magne-
tite, not related to late magmatic alterations. The distribution of site means as well as the
change of directions of the rcmanence vectors during thermal demagnetization can be
explained by a slow rate of cooling and where signs of metamorphism exist by partial
remagnetization of the rock. This study has, apart from the palaeomagnetic results, demon-
strated the difficulty of correlating radiometric ages with agcs of magnctization. 0 Svccokar-

To reduce the possibility of oxidation of the
specimens these thermal demagnetizations were
carried out in argon gas. Temperature calibration
experiments in the TSD-1 furnace used indicate
the temperatures estimated to be accurate to
k 10°C.
Statistical analyses
Fisherian statistics are used to estimate the mean
directions of the sites and of the formation. To
avoid situations involving subjective judgement,
determinations of mean directions have been car-
ried out during the whole process of demagnet-
ization. Together with the demagnetization

Apart from the poles of the anomalous sites 3
+
and (1 6), the apparent palaeomagnetic poles
of the Svappavanrn gabbro are rather well con-
centrated forming mean with high precision at
235"E and'52"N (Fig. 6, Table 5).
The rather unstable remanence of Site 3 gives
a pole position 30 degrees west of the formation
mean (Fig. 6), a position similar to the poles of
the basic rocks at Sangis and the single 'meta-
morphic' pole of Nottrask. As poles of younger
rocks are found further west the rock at site 3
seems to have been magnetized at a later orogen-
ic stage.
The directional changes during the stepwise
thermal demagnetization indicate a backward cx-
tension 'of the apparent polar wandering path
quite similar to that found for the Tarendo gab-
bro. The difference in radiometric ages of the
surrounding rocks, U-Pb = 1880-1860 Ma and
x Notlrosk Svoppovaora
Rb-Sr 1780, 1725 Ma is either a proof of a very Sangis 8+ Viltangi
slow rate of uplift and cooling or an influence of A Tarendo Dundret
a serorogene metamorphic event. As for the Fig. 7. Site mean directions of all sites in this study.
Tarendo gabbro a slow cooling of the Svappa-
vaara gabbro is indicated by myrmekite textures.
The similarity in pole position and thermal be-
haviour of these two gabbros indicates them to
be magnetized at the same time and under simi-
lar circumstances. The age of magnetization is
therefore to be found in the time range
FORMATION MEANS
1880- 1725 Ma. The pole position of the well-
defined mean of Site 1 (and 6) situated at a
latitude, not obtained from any other formation
cannot be explained at present.
Also in the Viffarzgig abbro an east-west distri-
bution of the apparent site mean pole position is
obvious (Fig. 6, Table 6).
Contrary to the Svappavaara and Tiirendo
gabbros the thermal demagnetization of Vittangi
samples does not show any high Curie tempera-
ture components that can extend the path east-
ward. The well rounded shape of this massif, in
contrast to the shapes of the Svappavaara and
Tiirendo massifs, might indicate a later intrusion
of this rock and therefore no record of older
palaeofield similar to that of the other two rocks
is obtained. The same mineralogical signs of slow
cooling are also found in this rock and the age of
magnetization is probably similar but somewhat
younger than for Svappavaara and TirendLi.
